chapter_title: The Mathematics of Maybe: Introduction to Probability
key_takeaways: Probability quantifies chance on a scale from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain).
Experimental probability relies on real trial data (P = favorable trials / total trials) and approaches theoretical probability as trials increase.
Theoretical probability assumes equally likely outcomes and calculates P = favorable outcomes / total outcomes.
A sample space S must contain all distinct possible outcomes without omission.
Tree diagrams and systematic tables prevent missing outcomes in multi-stage experiments (coin tosses, dice rolls).
Geometric probability extends chance measurement to spatial areas and regions.
